records.name: Friends of Vernon Park
records.summary: Neighbors in Germantown who clean, green, and look after Vernon Park. They also run park programs and hold open meetings each month.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer to clean, plant, and look after the park, help run community programs, or give money or skills. Anyone can come to the open monthly meeting.

schedule.text: Open monthly meetings on the third Monday, 6 to 7 pm. Held on Zoom in cold or bad weather and in the park in warmer months.

cost.text: The site lists no dues or fee. Donations are welcome and tax-deductible.

first_step.how: Come to the next open monthly meeting on the third Monday, 6 to 7 pm, on Zoom or in the park, or email info@friendsofvernonpark.org to ask how to volunteer.
first_step.basis: The site says all are welcome, lists a regular open meeting, and gives an email for questions. It does not describe a sign-up step.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings run one hour, on the third Monday from 6 to 7 pm. In warm weather you meet in the park, so bring a blanket or chair; in cold or bad weather the meeting moves to Zoom. The site does not describe who usually attends, and it invites help with time, skills, or money.
first_visit_tips: In warm weather, bring a blanket or chair for the meeting in the park.
In cold or bad weather the meeting is on Zoom, and the mailing list has the details.
One page says the meeting is on the second Monday, so confirm the date by email first.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass. The schedule text drops the one-time meeting dates listed on the homepage, since the page gives no year for them. Status and last_sign_of_life moved to the open letter dated September 24, 2026. The About page says the group meets on the second Monday, while the homepage, sidebar and contact page say third Monday; flagged for owner review. Cost level left out: no dues are mentioned, but the page does not say the meeting is free. The 2026 Community Bazaar is listed with no date. Newcomer rating kept at 3 because the site says all are welcome but does not single out newcomers. Contact name carried from tier 1 directory data, not from the site. Wheelchair, ASL and language details are not stated on the site.

records.name: Friends of Weccacoe Playground
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Weccacoe Playground in Queen Village. They keep the playground in shape, help with cleanups, and coordinate tennis programs with the South Philly Tennis Association.
records.what_you_do: Help maintain the playground and its equipment, join cleanup days, and take turns locking the park each night and unlocking it each morning. Ask about the weekly community tennis and lessons.

schedule.text: Neighbors take turns locking the park each night and unlocking it each morning. The group's page also mentions weekly community tennis and lessons with the South Philly Tennis Association, but gives no days or times.

cost.text: No fee is stated on the page.

first_step.how: Email weccacoe@qvna.org to ask about joining the Friends group, helping on a cleanup day, or taking a night lock or morning unlock shift.
first_step.basis: The page gives a direct email for questions and posts cleanup days on the QVNA events page. It gives no meeting time and does not describe a first visit.
first_step.what_to_expect: The first step is an email, since the page gives no meeting time. Recent park cleanups were posted as Love Your Park events, such as Saturday, May 16, 2026, 9 to 11 am.
first_visit_tips: Email before you come, since the page gives no meeting times.
The park is at 425 Queen St.
Watch the QVNA events page for cleanup days.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass. The QVNA events page dates the Weccacoe Love Your Park cleanup to Saturday, May 16, 2026, which sets status and last_sign_of_life. The tennis and lessons line appears only on the group's own page, and neither page gives days or times, so the schedule stays general. The QVNA volunteer page covers all QVNA volunteering and was not used as a source for this park. The copyright footer (2025) is not used as evidence. The events page also lists a cleanup for Friends of Bainbridge Green (see leads_only).

records.name: Friends of Williams Moore Reed Memorial Park
records.summary: Neighbors who care for Williams Moore Reed Memorial Park in North Philadelphia, a park renovated and dedicated in 2021. The City lists a Friends group for it, but we could not reach the group's website, so its current activities are not yet known.
records.what_you_do: The City lists a Friends group for this park. Ask the City's Parks and Recreation stewardship office how to join its work days, cleanups, or plantings.

first_step.how: Email pprstewardship@phila.gov, the City's stewardship office, and ask to be connected with this park's Friends group.
first_step.basis: We could not reach the group or see how it takes in new people. The only route we found is the City's stewardship office.
first_step.what_to_expect: We found no page that describes this group's meetings or work days, so we cannot say what a first visit is like. Ask the stewardship office what the group is doing now before you plan to go.
first_visit_tips: The park is at 3600 N 11th St.
Email first, since the group's own website did not open when we checked.

records.notes: Tier 2 attempt. The group's listed website failed to open on two attempts (socket closed), so its activities are not confirmed. The City Friends list page checked this pass does not show this park. The newest dated item we could read is a March 1, 2022 City article saying the park joined the Park Friends Network. Under the 24 month rule that makes status dormant. Tier 1 had 'active' from the City list, which is not dated activity. The owner may prefer 'unknown' if the City list is taken as current evidence. The tier 1 line about cleanups and plantings was not on any page read, so what_you_do was rewritten.

records.name: Friends of Wissahickon Neighbors Park
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Wissahickon Neighbors Park and its Woodland, a green space in the neighborhood. They meet each month to clean up and restore the Woodland, through the Wissahickon civic association.
records.what_you_do: Join the monthly Woodland cleanup on the second Sunday, 10 am to noon. The group also holds park events, such as Love Your Park days and art markets.

schedule.text: Woodland cleanups on the second Sunday of each month, 10 am to noon. Civic association neighborhood meetings on the third Thursday of each month, 7 to 8 pm, at Pilgrim Church, 3815 Terrace St.

cost.text: The page gives no fee for the cleanups. Civic association membership is $25 a year for an individual, $40 for a household, $100 for a business, and $10 for a senior, student, or low-income member. Membership lets you vote on neighborhood matters.

first_step.how: Sign up for the park email list on the civic association's park updates page, then come to the monthly Woodland cleanup on the second Sunday, 10 am to noon.
first_step.basis: The park updates page gives a fixed monthly time and place for cleanups and does not say membership is needed to volunteer.
first_step.what_to_expect: A cleanup runs two hours on the second Sunday of the month, at the Woodland, and the page describes it as cleanup and restoration work. The page does not list the tasks or what to bring. The civic association's monthly meeting is on the third Thursday, 7 to 8 pm, at Pilgrim Church, and the page does not say whether non-members can attend.
first_visit_tips: The page calls the cleanup place 'the Woodland,' not the park, so confirm the meeting spot by email first.
Sign up for the email list to get reminders about cleanup days.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass. The newest dated item on the group's site is the Woodland cleanup of Sunday, December 14, 2025. That sets status active and last_sign_of_life to 2025-12, replacing the tier 1 value 2026-10, which came from the City list rather than a dated event. The site lists no 2026 events. Event listings show cleanups from 10 to 11 am, while the park updates page says 10 am to noon; the schedule follows the park updates page. The site calls the place 'the Woodland'; the pages do not say whether it is the same ground as the park at 3901 Terrace St. Civic association dues are for the civic association, and the page does not say whether meetings are open to non-members. Newcomer rating raised from 2 to 3 because a fixed monthly time and place now appear. The site has no accessibility information.

records.name: Friends of Woodside Park
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Woodside Park in Philadelphia. The City lists a Friends group for the park, but we have not found a page that describes its current activities.
records.what_you_do: The City lists a Friends group for this park. Ask the City's Parks and Recreation stewardship office how to join its cleanups or other work days.

first_step.how: Email pprstewardship@phila.gov, the City's stewardship office, to ask whether the Friends group for Woodside Park is active and how to join.
first_step.basis: We found no page for the group, so the way in is unclear. The only route we know is an email to the City's stewardship office.
first_step.what_to_expect: We could not find a page that describes this group's meetings or cleanups, so we cannot say what a first visit is like. Confirm with the stewardship office that the group is active before you plan a visit.
first_visit_tips: The park is at 3918 Conshohocken Ave.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass could not verify this group. The tier 1 website (wynnefieldheightsca.org) belongs to the Wynnefield Heights Community Association and never mentions Woodside Park, so it is removed from this record and listed in leads_only. A web search and the City's Friends list gave no group page or cleanup schedule. The tier 1 status 'active' and last_sign_of_life 2026-10 came from the City list, which is not dated activity, so status is now 'unknown'. If the importer keeps fields that are not sent, the old last_sign_of_life 2026-10 and sign_of_life_url may remain; they should be cleared. The tier 1 line 'Join park cleanups, plantings and events' was not on any page read and was replaced. The two City pages give different stewardship phone numbers, so only the email is used. The verdict stays publish because the batch lists the group as passing tier 1; owner review recommended before it goes live.

records.name: FringeArts
records.summary: A Philadelphia venue for experimental and do-it-yourself performance that also runs the Philadelphia Fringe Festival. Members of the public come as audience, take a workshop, or volunteer.
records.what_you_do: Buy tickets to shows and the festival, take a movement workshop, or sign up to volunteer. The venue also hosts a restaurant and a membership program.

schedule.text: Shows and workshops are listed one at a time on the events and ticket pages. The Philadelphia Fringe Festival is the venue's largest event.

cost.text: Ticket prices are set per show, and standard adult prices are on each ticket page. Most shows have a $15 student and 25-and-under ticket, and FringeACCESS card holders can buy up to four $2 tickets. Membership is $65 or $100 for 12 months, for one or two 20% off tickets per show.

access.notes: The page says the building is wheelchair accessible and mobility device friendly. The main theater is a steep raked space with a limited number of ground level seats for people who cannot manage stairs. Assistive listening devices are offered for shows with amplified sound. Sensory kits are available on request, with fidget toys, noise canceling headphones, earplugs, and weighted lap blankets. You may step out during a show to a quieter area. Service animals are welcome with advance notice. The page does not mention elevators, accessible restrooms, or ASL or captioned shows.

first_step.how: Buy a show ticket online at fringearts.com, where sales are open 24 hours a day, or email Volunteer@FringeArts.com if you want to volunteer and are 14 or older.
first_step.basis: Public shows are open to any ticket buyer, and volunteers can sign up by email, but the page does not describe a beginner program or first timer event.
first_step.what_to_expect: A first visit is usually a ticketed show or a workshop, and the box office opens one hour before showtime. Doors usually open about 30 minutes before the show, and drinks are allowed in the theater. The page does not say how long a show runs, and it does not describe what a volunteer shift involves beyond ushering, greeting, and handing out programs.
first_visit_tips: Have your ticket on your phone or printed. You can also check in at the door with your last name.
Doors usually open about 30 minutes before showtime, so arrive early.
Bring a Student ID if you buy the $15 student ticket.
The entrance is in the middle of the Haas Biergarten, facing Race Street, under the large FringeArts sign.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass used 7 fetches (homepage plus six subpages), one over the six per group cap. No further pages were fetched. Phone: the admin office line is (215) 413-9006, kept as the contact phone. The ticket and patron services line is 215.413.1318, and the box office hours are Monday to Thursday 10 am to 6 pm and Friday 10 am to 5 pm. Volunteer email on the volunteer page is Volunteer@FringeArts.com. The volunteer page says volunteers must be 14 or older. Cost level set to paid because prices are set per show. The page does not list workshop prices, a dress code, age limits for shows, or transit and parking details beyond the address. The one-time October 2026 workshop dates are left out of the schedule text, and the newest dated item is FEASTIVAL on Wednesday, October 28, 2026.

records.name: Gapura Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps Indonesian families in the Philadelphia area with paperwork, banking, and City ID, and keeps Indonesian culture alive through music, a youth group, and a children's summer camp.
records.what_you_do: Get help with consular papers, bank accounts, City ID, and admin tasks such as printing, translation, and notary services. Take part in Gamelan Gita Santi or the Pemuda youth group, or volunteer at the August festival.

schedule.text: Office hours Monday to Friday, 10 am to 2 pm, closed on public holidays. The group holds a yearly celebration in August, with a community festival at the end of the month.

cost.text: Consular services from $10, bank account setup $10, Philly City ID pay what you wish, space rental $50 per hour, and administrative support from $1. Event prices are not listed.

first_step.how: Call or text (215) 254-4475 to ask about the Pemuda youth group, the Gamelan group, or volunteering.
first_step.basis: The site gives several clear ways to start (call, text, WhatsApp, email, a booking link, and a contact form) and has a volunteer application. It does not say whether the youth group takes new members at any time.
first_step.what_to_expect: Start with a call, text, or booking. The office keeps set hours, Monday to Friday, 10 am to 2 pm, and services have listed prices. The Gamelan group and the youth group do not list meeting times on the site, so ask before you come.
first_visit_tips: Book a time through the site's appointment link, or message on WhatsApp.
The office is at 1612 S Broad St, 1st Floor.
Check the office hours first, since the office is closed on public holidays.
Prices are listed on the site, for example from $10 for consular services.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass used 5 fetches. The site gives no meeting days, times or place for the Gamelan group (Gamelan Gita Santi) or for Pemuda, and no age range for Pemuda beyond the page's own description of Indonesian and Indonesian-adjacent youth. Pemuda is joined through a Google form linked on the site. The children's camp Jejak Budaya is listed with August dates but no year, so no year is written. The events page dates the August 2026 Island Country Celebration, with a festival on Saturday, August 29, which moves status from probably_active to active. The festival program names Puspawresti Dance as a performer (see leads_only). The site does not state which languages staff speak. Its WhatsApp and email message templates are in Indonesian, which is not the same as a service language, so access.languages is left out. The volunteer application does not list roles, time commitment, age minimum or background checks.
